comment: Cancel conformance fixture (SPEC.md 10.8, 10.8a, 7.3, 19.2). Pins the bytes where two independent implementations drift: the eight reason strings, the cancel-request payload shape, the canceled task-update payload shape, the failed task-update payload shape, the unmet_need reference format, the propagated-cancel shape (reason upstream_cancelled, original reason carried in the note) and the exact note format, and the reject cases (unknown reason, missing reason, unbacked needs_not_furnished). Both SDKs implement this as of 2026-08-09. THE FIXTURE IS THE AUTHORITY: when a test against it fails, fix the implementation, and when the fixture itself is believed wrong, change it only with a spec change alongside.

identities.comment: The same published test vectors budget.json and inbound-protections.json use, deliberately: they are not real identities and control nothing, and reusing them keeps any new private-key-shaped string out of the repository.

reasons.comment: 10.8: reason is REQUIRED on a cancel and the enum is CLOSED - a cancel whose reason is missing or not one of these eight exact strings is rejected as INVALID_ENVELOPE. The strings are the wire bytes; the descriptions are informative. deadline_exceeded and budget_exhausted deliberately reuse the 12.2 vocabulary so a cancel after an overdue mark or a budget pause reads consistently with the budget lifecycle (7.7). needs_not_furnished and dependency_failed joined the enum 2026-08-09 so that a failure that was not the provider's doing, and a failure caused by a dependency the provider chose, stop looking identical to a provider that simply did not deliver (10.8a).

descriptions.user_requested: a human, or the requesting agent's own logic, decided the work is no longer wanted
descriptions.superseded: a newer request replaces this one; the answer would be discarded even if delivered
descriptions.deadline_exceeded: the budget's deadline (7.7) passed and the requester chose to stop rather than keep listening
descriptions.budget_exhausted: the cost ceiling was reached (7.7 pause) and the requester chose to cancel rather than raise the budget
descriptions.upstream_cancelled: the canceling agent's own Task was canceled and it is forwarding the cancellation to a delegate
descriptions.policy: an operator or policy layer terminated the work on content, permission, or tenancy grounds
descriptions.needs_not_furnished: the caller did not furnish something the offering declared under needs (8.5.1); REQUIRES unmet_need
descriptions.dependency_failed: an outside service the responder depends on, and should have declared under works_with (8.8), stopped working; SHOULD carry dependency

unmet_need.comment: 10.8: unmet_need is REQUIRED with needs_not_furnished and MUST NOT appear with any other reason. Format is '<kind>:<value>' where kind is one of the four 8.5.1 need kinds and value is that entry's own value. The colon splits at the FIRST colon only - a value may contain colons.

attribution.comment: 10.8a: the platform COMPUTES attribution on the terminal failed event and a party never asserts it. 'client' requires BOTH the needs_not_furnished reason AND an unmet_need that names a need actually declared on the responder's registered manifest (8.5.1). Everything else is 'provider', including an unbacked claim and a claim that could not be checked - a provider must not be able to buy a clean record with an assertion, nor profit from a registry outage. dependency_failed is 'provider' on purpose: the provider chose the dependency.

cases.why: the claim names nothing the offering ever declared, so it is an assertion and not evidence
null means the manifest could not be read; an unverifiable claim fails closed
the buyer's work did not get done and the provider picked the dependency; the separate reason buys legibility, not absolution
a failure with no reason is a complete statement and stays the provider's
an attribution field in a party's payload is not an input

shapes.comment: 10.8: a cancel travels twice. (1) The task.cancel REQUEST to the performer's inbox: payload.offering 'task.cancel', payload.input carrying task_id + reason + optional note. (2) The canceled TASK UPDATE (a respond on mesh.task.{task_id}.update): payload.status 'canceled' with the same reason + optional note alongside it. The note is OPTIONAL free text and is OMITTED when absent, never null; the enum, not the note, is what the record carries as meaning.

failed_update_payload.note: the search form moved and the wrapper cannot read it

propagation.comment: 10.8: an agent that delegated part of a live Task and receives a cancel for it forwards a cancel to each still-live delegate with reason 'upstream_cancelled', carrying the ORIGINAL reason in the note. Note format, pinned: the original reason string alone when the original cancel had no note; otherwise the original reason, then ': ' (colon space), then the original note. Both SDKs must produce these exact bytes.

cases.why: propagation composes: a two-hop chain nests, and the reason stays upstream_cancelled at every hop

invalid.comment: 12.2 / 10.8: rejected as INVALID_ENVELOPE, at the door, before any state is touched. The task manager's door is fire-and-forget (warn-and-refuse, nothing persisted, nothing published); an SDK inbox replies with an INVALID_ENVELOPE error envelope where a reply is permitted.

cases.why: the enum is closed - a reason invented in the field is rejected, never recorded
reason is REQUIRED on every cancel
absent is omitted, never null - and even as presence, null is not one of the six strings
the strings are exact bytes; there is no case folding
note, when present, is a string
unmet_need is REQUIRED with this reason - a claim about the caller that names nothing is not checkable
unmet_need is '<kind>:<value>' with kind from the four 8.5.1 need kinds
unmet_need is meaningful with exactly one reason and MUST NOT ride any other
dependency is meaningful only with dependency_failed

envelope.comment: A fully-formed, really-signed task.cancel request using the published sender identity. 'canonical' is the canonical envelope JSON (SPEC.md 5.3) WITHOUT the domain prefix; the signature covers signed_bytes_prefix + canonical. Any conforming implementation MUST rebuild those bytes from the envelope and verify the signature; one changed byte of reason or note must fail verification.

input.note: re-planned; a broader query replaces this one

transitions.comment: 7.3: which states may cancel. The paused states can - 7.7's BUDGET_EXHAUSTED pause parks a Task in input_required precisely so the requester can revise the budget OR cancel and keep the partial artifacts. Terminal states cannot (TASK_NOT_CANCELABLE). `exhausted` joined the terminal side with Agent SoW 0.4.0-draft 5.5.5 (agentsow.com): under a time and materials arrangement a task in flight when the engagement's not-to-exceed cap is reached ends `exhausted`, with whatever artifacts exist attached. It is terminal and it is NOT a failure - the cancel that would have been offered has already happened.

not_covered.comment: Boundaries, written down so nobody mistakes them for gaps.
items: Whether a performer actually PROPAGATES is unverifiable by design (10.8: the MUST is honor-system inside the performer). This fixture pins the shapes a propagating implementation must produce; the teeth are the task manager's stranded-delegate flag (stranded: true + mesh.event.task.stranded), which is service behavior tested in services/, not here.

Computing attribution (10.8a) needs the responder's registered manifest, which no SDK holds. The attribution cases above pin the DECISION given a declared-needs list, and the platform-side lookup that produces that list is service behavior tested in services/, not here.
There is deliberately NO bounded acknowledgement to pin: for the requester, cancellation is effective when sent, and delivery to the performer is on mailbox time (10.8).
The canceled metering receipt (19.2: mesh.event.metering.task_canceled, cancel_reason) is the task manager's emission, tested in services/, not an SDK wire shape.
